sam (support): Heads-up — customer 'acme-corp' opened a critical support ticket after Friday's pen test. They saw intermittent 403s on /v1/generate and provided a CloudTrail extract. Escalating here for triage.

maria (sec): Thanks. Can you paste the customer repro steps + the CloudTrail lines (sanitized) and the exact error body? Also: which KMS key is attached to that tenant?

sam (support): Repro steps they sent:
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" -H \"X-Tenant-ID: acme-staging\" -d '{"prompt":"test"}' https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```
Response snippet (sanitized):
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "access_denied",
  "message": "KMS:NotAuthorized to use key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-efgh",
  "x-request-id": "req-abc123"
}
```
They say ~1/40 calls fail, all from their staging tenant. KMS key ID attached to tenant: alias/redwood/acme-staging. CloudTrail event they attached shows a ListAliases and a Decrypt call from an IP owned by the pen-test runner during testing.

kai (infra): Hmm. Intermittent 403 with KMS NotAuthorized suggests either a policy race or a fallback path hitting a different principal. Attach the key policy and IAM role used by the runtime? Also enable CloudTrail lookup for events with RequestID req-abc123.

sam (support): Pasted cloudtrail lines (sanitized):
```
{ "eventTime": "2026-03-12T18:02:11Z", "eventName": "ListAliases", "userIdentity": { "type": "AssumedRole", "arn": "arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/redwood-runtime/instance-123" }, "sourceIPAddress": "54.36.21.100" }
{ "eventTime": "2026-03-12T18:02:12Z", "eventName": "Decrypt", "userIdentity": { "type": "AssumedRole", "arn": "arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/redwood-runtime/instance-123" }, "errorMessage": "Not authorized to use key" }
```

maria (sec): If ListAliases is present from the runtime role, that's odd — ListAliases shouldn't be needed for normal decrypt; could indicate a dynamic alias lookup path that the runtime uses when a cache miss occurs. That could be triggered during cold starts or after rotation.

olivia (sre): Two threads to run in parallel: 1) Reproduce locally with same tenant config and the same assumed-role creds (we can create a test role scoped to the runtime role). 2) Inspect the key policy for any Allow to "*" or conditions that could let a different principal attempt enumeration. Also check if we recently pushed any KMS SDK change (we did bump aws-sdk-go last week).

pen-test-bot: Pen test issue #345 created. Severity proposed by external tester: Low. Evidence attached: cloudtrail snippet + HTTP 403s. Link: https://pen-tests.example.com/345

maria (sec): I disagree with Low. Potential impact: data-decryption failures for tenant traffic and possible key enumeration. Propose Medium until we rule out policy/privilege escalation. We need reproducible steps and proof that the key policy allowed unintended ListAliases or Decrypt.

kai (infra): I pulled the key policy for alias/redwood/acme-staging — there was a recent change on 2026-03-10 where a temporary permissive statement was added by infra-automation to help a migration:
```
{ "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": "*", "Action": ["kms:ListAliases"], "Resource": "*" }
```
(yes, sorry, that was the automation). That explains the ListAliases call but shouldn't cause Decrypt NotAuthorized unless the Decrypt call came from a different principal that lacks explicit Allow. Looks like the runtime role relies on IAM allow + key policy allow. If the policy was permissive for ListAliases but not Decrypt, Decrypt could fail when role session is unexpected.

maria (sec): Okay — this is actionable. Change the policy to remove the public ListAliases Allow and instead restrict to the runtime role and the infra automation principal. Also add conditions: aws:SourceIp and aws:PrincipalTag for environment.

kai (infra): Proposed fix (will run after approvals):
```
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id alias/redwood/acme-staging --policy file://acme-staging-restricted-policy.json
```
policy snippet we'll apply:
```
Allow Principal: arn:aws:iam::123456:role/redwood-runtime Action: kms:Decrypt kms:GenerateDataKey Resource: * Condition: StringEquals aws:PrincipalTag/tenant: acme-staging
Deny Principal: * Action: kms:ListAliases Resource: * Condition: Null aws:PrincipalTag/tenant
```

sam (support): Pen test team asked for retest after we apply the change. They also requested full CloudTrail evidence that ListAliases was possible from the runtime before we change things. I attached the events to the pen issue.

maria (sec): Severity decision: Medium for now. If pen team can demonstrate an unauthenticated principal obtained alias metadata or there is evidence of key material access, we escalate to High.

olivia (sre): Also enable CloudTrail Insight for KMS and set up short-term enhanced logging for that key (data plane events to S3) so we have richer evidence during retest. I'll create a runbook snippet for on-call if we see elevated 5xx/403 rate for that tenant.

sam (support): Scheduled retest: pen team confirmed retest window 2026-03-15 16:00 UTC. I'll be on the call to gather HTTP traces and OIDC tokens. Action owners: kai -> apply policy + notify when done; olivia -> enable enhanced audit; maria -> triage severity and update pen issue.

pen-test-bot: Pen test issue #345 updated: status=Awaiting Retest.

maria (sec): After retest, we need the following evidence to close: 1) CloudTrail full events for the retest window, 2) sanitized HTTP request/response including X-Request-ID, 3) confirmation the key policy change is in place (policy diff), 4) post-fix 72h monitoring showing zero KMS NotAuthorized errors for that tenant.

sam (support): Understood. I'll collect and attach everything. For now we're not notifying customers beyond the affected staging tenant.

kai (infra): Policy change applied at 2026-03-12T20:05:02Z. I pushed the restricted policy, added a deny for ListAliases to non-tagged principals, and rolled it through our canary region. Rolling to prod after verification.

olivia (sre): Enhanced KMS logging enabled for alias/redwood/acme-staging at 2026-03-12T20:10Z. Watchers set.

sam (support): Pen test retest completed at 2026-03-15T16:12:40Z. Pen team reports: no reproducible 403s during 1hr retest. They uploaded CloudTrail events showing failed ListAliases attempts from their test runner but those were blocked after the policy change.

maria (sec): Reviewing artifacts now. Initial check: key policy diff looks correct, CloudTrail shows the ListAliases calls prior to policy change and denies afterward. Severity downgraded to Low with note: misconfiguration introduced by infra automation. Recommendation: tighten automation to never apply wildcard KMS ListAliases and add a pre-deploy policy lint.

pen-test-bot: Pen test issue #345 closed by pen team: Resolved (Low). Evidence linked.

sam (support): Closing internal ticket after 72h observation window. Customer staging confirmed no more 403s. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
